title: Mitigate pager fatigue via burn-window and sensitivity tuning after multi-region capacity regression
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Follow-up from the 2026-02-06 multi-region capacity regression that caused sustained 5xx increase and multiple burn-rate pages. Investigation showed: (1) burn-rate alert windows were configured at 5m/15m which produced noisy, non-actionable pages during short-lived capacity pressure; (2) pager thresholds are uniform across tiers and regions, so regional spikes in non-critical customers escalated to P0/P1 pages unnecessarily; (3) there is no adaptive suppression for autoscaling events or known maintenance windows. This ticket captures action items to reduce alert noise, tighten signal fidelity, and prevent unnecessary on-call load while preserving SLO safety.
tasks: Audit current burn-rate and error-rate alert configs (all regions and tiers) and produce a spreadsheet of windows, thresholds, and pager targets
Increase short-window burn-rate aggregation from 5m -> 10m and medium from 15m -> 30m for non-critical tiers; run retrospective on false-positive rate before apply
Introduce tier-aware pager thresholds: map P0/P1 only to customer-impacting routes and global control plane paths; demote noisy customer tenants to non-pager alerting streams
Add autoscaling and deployment event signals to suppression rules (k8s rollout, Dedicated autoscale events) so expected transient errors don't page
Implement adaptive cooldown: if burn-rate triggers coincide with known capacity autoscale, delay pager for 2m and raise synthetic checks for escalation
Create canary rollout for new config in staging -> us-east -> global with metric-backed rollback criteria
Update on-call runbook and playbook with new thresholds, suppression logic, and troubleshooting steps
Add synthetic load tests to CI that simulate regional capacity spikes and validate that only real degradations page
acceptance_criteria: Pager count (P0/P1) attributable to burn-rate alerts is reduced by at least 60% in the following 14 days post-rollout for non-critical routes
No change to customer-visible SLO breaches (total breach rate) beyond a 5% variance after new rules are applied
Automated suppression does not mask genuine outages: synthetic failover test triggers a page within configured escalation window
Runbook updated and on-call team trained; at least two runbook-driven incident responses completed successfully in staging
